claim: Each stage of a three-stage post-training pipeline (continual pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning) is necessary for balancing domain expertise enhancement with general ability retention.
falsifier: Apply the pipeline with one stage removed (e.g., skip CPT or SFT or RL) and measure domain expertise and general ability; verify that removal of any stage degrades the balance.

conditions: domain-specific data used in each stage
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system (FitOne-8B based on Qwen3-8B), task (SFC certification exams), and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Three-stage post-training pipeline for balance between domain expertise

claim: Post-training-induced geopolitical bias in large language models can be decomposed into architectural and reasoning-specific components, as revealed by a neutral-filler control that separates the effect of the model's own reasoning from other factors.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by applying the neutral-filler control to other post-trained LLMs to decompose bias sources.

conditions: evaluated using forced-choice probes with a neutral-filler control
tested on GLM 4 and Gemma models
observed that for GLM, amplification is reasoning-specific; for Gemma, both architectural and reasoning components exist
exclusions: limited to the two model families tested (GLM 4 and Gemma)
limited to the neutral-filler control methodology
transferability to other models is unestablished

title: Post-training–geopolitical bias decomposed into mechanism
